chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Humayd, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have been appointed toiled with a job/work, so is there an exit for me from that?' He said, 'How many are those who seek an exit from that but it becomes difficult for them.' I said, 'So what do you see?' He said, 'I see that you should fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not repeat it.'

key_terms.وُلِّيتُ عَمَلًا: I was appointed to a job/work

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on holding government office according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the dilemma of holding public office under unjust rulers, a common concern in Shia political jurisprudence. Rather than commanding immediate resignation, he advises Taqwa (God-consciousness) and steadfastness, suggesting that the spiritual burden of the role is manageable if one remains mindful of Allah. This reflects the pragmatic Shia approach to engagement with authority, prioritizing internal piety and duty over mere positional exit.
